original_question: For the Kuramoto-type global synchronization notion where a graph is globally synchronizing when all local minima of E(theta) = (1/2) sum_{i,j=1}^n Aij(1 - cos(theta_i - theta_j)) are global minima at constant phases, is the following extremal statement true: for every epsilon > 0 there exists n and an n-vertex graph G with minimum degree at least (3/4 - epsilon)n that is not globally synchronizing?
target_in_paper: Entry 2, "Global Synchronization": Definition 2.1 together with Conjecture 5 ("Density threshold for Global Synchrony").
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s official formulation. It uses the same Kuramoto energy, the same notion of global synchronization as a statement about local minima versus global constant-phase minima, the same extremal minimum-degree threshold ((3/4) - ε)n, and the same existential quantifier pattern "for every ε > 0 there exists n and a graph G" that appears in the paper’s Conjecture 5.
missing_details: The paper phrases the question explicitly for a graph G on n nodes, with A being the adjacency matrix of G.
The paper’s definition first introduces global synchronization for an n×n matrix A and then transfers the notion to graphs via their adjacency matrices.
The phase variables are taken in the Kuramoto configuration space parameterized by θ ∈ [0, 2π)^n; the draft does not explicitly say over what domain local minima are taken.
To make the question fully stand-alone, one should unpack "not globally synchronizing" as: the energy has at least one local minimum that is not a global constant-phase minimum.
The paper presents this specifically as the "extremal combinatorics" version of the global synchrony problem, so naming it as a density-threshold question makes the scope sharper.
The precise quantifier in the paper is "there exists n > 0 and a graph G on n nodes"; writing "there exists a positive integer n" makes this mathematically explicit.
refined_question: Is the following density-threshold conjecture for Kuramoto global synchrony true? For every ε > 0, does there exist a positive integer n and an n-vertex graph G with adjacency matrix A and minimum degree δ(G) ≥ (3/4 - ε)n such that the Kuramoto energy E(θ) = (1/2) ∑_{i,j=1}^n A_{ij}(1 - cos(θ_i - θ_j)) on phase configurations θ ∈ [0, 2π)^n has a local minimum that is not a global constant-phase minimum θ1 = ··· = θn = c?
justification: The draft is targeting the paper’s Entry 2 on global synchronization, not a broader neighboring problem. The paper first defines a matrix/graph to be globally synchronizing in Definition 2.1 by means of the Kuramoto energy and the requirement that the only local minima are the global constant-phase minima. It then states exactly the extremal minimum-degree question as Conjecture 5, titled "Density threshold for Global Synchrony," on printed page 3. The surrounding sentence immediately before Conjecture 5 says this is the "extremal combinatorics" version of the question, and the sentence immediately after it says earlier work gives an upper bound and evidence that 3/4 is the correct threshold. Also, for the supplied arXiv paper 2504.20539, there is no relevant Conjecture 1.1 / Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3; the relevant official formulation is Definition 2.1 plus Conjecture 5 in Entry 2.
